newsitem.title: USA: PGE files direct access plan with Ore. regulators.
newsitem.headline: PGE files direct access plan with Ore. regulators.

text.p: Portland General Electric Co (PGE) said Wednesday it filed a plan to allow large industrial and commercial customers to buy up to one-third of their electricity needs from any supplier.
The new tariff will take effect upon approval by the Oregon Public Utility Commission (OPUC), the utility said.
Portland General also said it plans to launch a second program next year to allow about 50,000 residential and small commercial customers to choose their electricity provider.
Filings for the second program will be made in March.

Customers eliglible for the new tariff include large manufacturers, retail chains and hospitals with combined electricity demands of at least five megawatts (MW) during peak usage. It will initially be available for up to 75 MW of load per year.
The utility noted that if the OPUC approves its merger with Enron Corp, affected customers will be allowed to purchase 100 percent of their electricity through the tariff, up to 225 MW per year.
